ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A rectangular wooden box with a length of $L=1.5\mathrm{m}$, a height of $h=0.45\mathrm{m}$, and a mass of $M=10\mathrm{kg}$ is undergoing rectilinear motion to the right on a horizontal surface. When the velocity of the box is $v_0=3.6\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, a constant force $F=50\mathrm{N}$ is applied horizontally to the left on the box. Simultaneously, a small ball with a mass of $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is gently placed at point $P$, which is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the length from the right end of the box (the ball can be considered a point mass, and its initial velocity relative to the ground is zero when placed at point $P$). The coefficient of kinetic friction between the box and the ground is 0.2, and all other frictions are negligible. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The time it takes for the small ball to fall to the ground from the moment it leaves the box.
2. Determine the maximum displacement of the wooden box to the right after the small ball is placed at point $P$.
3. Find the velocity of the wooden box at the moment the small ball leaves the box.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a rectangular wooden box placed on a horizontal ground with diagonal-line shading; on the upper surface of the wooden box there is a small ball, labeled P, located at a position slightly to the right on the box top; on the right side of the wooden box there is a velocity arrow v0 pointing to the right; on the left side there is a horizontal external force arrow F pointing to the left. The structure in the figure is consistent with the meaning of the problem: the box moves to the right on a rough horizontal surface, the external force is to the left, and the small ball is placed at point P on the box top. Reasoning: Take the horizontal rightward direction as the positive direction. There is no friction between the small ball and the wooden box, so the small ball is not subjected to force in the horizontal direction; when the small ball is gently placed, its initial velocity relative to the ground is 0, so while it is still on the box surface, its horizontal position relative to the ground remains unchanged. After the small ball is placed on it, during the stage in which the wooden box is still moving to the right, the direction of the kinetic friction force exerted by the ground on the wooden box is to the left, and the external force F is also to the left. Although the small ball does not exert a horizontal friction force on the wooden box, it increases the normal pressure of the wooden box on the ground, so the magnitude of the friction force exerted by the ground on the wooden box is μ(M+m)g = 0.2 × (10+1) × 10 = 22 N. The mass of the wooden box is M=10 kg, so the acceleration of the wooden box is a1 = -(F + μ(M+m)g)/M = -(50+22)/10 = -7.2 m/s^2. The displacement of the wooden box decelerating from the initial velocity v0=3.6 m/s to rest is s_stop = v0^2/(2×7.2) = 3.6^2/14.4 = 0.9 m. Therefore the maximum displacement of the wooden box to the right is 0.9 m. Point P is L/3 from the right end, so it is 2L/3 = 2×1.5/3 = 1.0 m from the left end. Since when the wooden box stops it has only moved 0.9 m to the right, the position of the small ball relative to the box has not yet reached the left edge, so the small ball has not yet left the wooden box. After the wooden box stops, under the action of the external force F it begins to move to the left. At this time the velocity of the wooden box is to the left, the direction of the kinetic friction force exerted by the ground on the wooden box is to the right, while the external force F is to the left, so the acceleration of the wooden box is a2 = -(F - μ(M+m)g)/M = -(50-22)/10 = -2.8 m/s^2. Let the displacement of the wooden box when the small ball is placed on it be x=0, and the initial position of the small ball be 1.0 m from the left end of the wooden box. The horizontal position of the small ball relative to the ground remains unchanged, and after the wooden box moves to the left, the small ball will leave from the right end of the wooden box. When it leaves the right end, the distance of the small ball relative to the left end of the wooden box is equal to L=1.5 m, so 1.0 - x = 1.5, giving x = -0.5 m. That is to say, from the rightmost position x=0.9 m of the wooden box to the time when the small ball leaves at x=-0.5 m, it needs to move 1.4 m to the left. Starting from rest, a2=-2.8 m/s^2, displacement Δx=-1.4 m, from v^2 = 2a2Δx we get v^2 = 2×(-2.8)×(-1.4)=7.84, so v = -2.8 m/s. The negative sign indicates the direction is to the left, therefore at the instant the small ball leaves the wooden box, the magnitude of the velocity of the wooden box is 2.8 m/s, directed to the left. After the small ball leaves the wooden box, it only undergoes vertical free-fall motion, and the height from the ground is h=0.45 m, so the falling time is t = sqrt(2h/g)=sqrt(2×0.45/10)=sqrt(0.09)=0.3 s.
